conservation.condition_narrative:
1992 – Frame was toned with microcrystalline wax and dry pigment. 
 
1994 – Surface cleaning to remove nicotine and grime layers from both canvas and frame; painting was keyed out to proper tension; replaced backing board with new sheet of Fome-cor and new hanging hardware was added to the stretcher. 
 
2014 – Painting was fitted into a microclimate enclosure; artwork was attached to a Dibond aluminum composite panel.
conservation.report_notes: Information provided for *Access O'Keeffe* by Hood Museum of Art in 2025 and reports conservation work from 1992, 1994, and 2014.

Signed on backing, in graphite: OK [in circle]; inscribed, on backing, in Alfred Stieglitz's hand: Near~~ Alcalde~~ [struckout] Taos Mountain [inserted as correction below "Near Alcalde," in O'Keeffe's hand?] - New Mexico - 1930 / by Georgia O'Keeffe; stamped twice on backing: ALFRED STIEGLITZ / LAKE GEORGE, N.Y.; label on backing stamped: AN AMERICAN PLACE / ROOM 1710-509 MADISON AVE. / NEW YORK, -N.Y. [and inscribed]: Georgia O'Keeffe 4 / 1930 / Taos Mountain - New Mexico [label is torn in lower right corner to remove price]; Downtown Gallery; label on backing printed: THE DOWNTOWN GALLERY . 32 E. 51st. ST., New York / ARTIST...GEORGIA O'KEEFFE..No...279 / TITLE ... TAOS MOUNTAIN, NEW MEXICO... DATE...1930...MEDIUM...OIL...SIZE...30x16 ...S.P>...; label on backing stamped: FINE ARTS CONSERVATION LABORATORIES [typed:] SPRAYED WITH: / Lucite #46, Acrylic Resin, Co. / polymer of N-Butyl and Isobutyl / Methacrylate. / April 1961. 
(Source: Hood Museum of Art, 2025)

cr_data.provenance:
Downtown Gallery, New York; sold to M. Rosalie Leidinger (1906-1991) and Louis W. Schmidt (1909-1995), Norwich, Vermont, 1961; given to present collection, 1993. 
(Source: Hood Museum of Art, 2025)
remarks_1999: Double entries Downtown Gallery Archive. Whitney Archive indicates, "Exam. at Amer. Place, March 1946. ... No signature [notes inscription 3]. Probably one of the Landscape toward Abiquiú series in 1931 exh." Abiquiú Notebooks after 1977 indicates, "Sold by Halpert ... April 18 1961." Pictured in 1931–32 New York (An American Place) Norman installation photograph, see Appendix III, figure 51A. (Source: Lynes, 1999)
